questions.question: Which of the following studies is considered the most powerful evidence-based study?
options: A multicenter double-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial
A meta-analysis of multiple longitudinal observational studies
questions.correctAnswer: A multicenter double-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial

questions.question: Which of the following order for the given studies represent a correct ranking with respect to an ascending order of evidence hierarchy (i.e., from lower evidence to higher evidence)?
options: case series, case report, nested case control, single subject randomized clinical trial, individual randomized controlled clinical trial, expert opinion
expert opinion, case report, case series, nested case control, individual randomized controlled clinical trial, single subject randomized clinical trial
case report, case series, expert opinion, nested case control, single subject randomized clinical trial, individual randomized controlled clinical trial
case report, case series, expert opinion, single subject randomized clinical trial, nested case control, individual randomized controlled clinical trial
questions.correctAnswer: expert opinion, case report, case series, nested case control, individual randomized controlled clinical trial, single subject randomized clinical trial

questions.question: Which of the following limitations does NOT represent a limitation associated with observational studies?
options: Associations between exposures and clinical outcomes do not establish causality
The lack of an observational study design that can efficiently assess incidence
End users may easily drift from associations to cause and effect
questions.correctAnswer: The lack of an observational study design that can efficiently assess incidence

To assess the efficacy of fluoxetine 80 mg/day on trichotillomania, 21 hair-puller adult patients were recruited into an 18-week small clinical trial. The patients were divided into 2 groups, in which the first group received the drug, whereas the second group received placebo for 6 weeks. Neither the patients nor the investigators know which is the drug or the placebo. After 5 weeks the first group received the placebo, whereas the second group received the drug. This study design is called:

Quespenem is a newly introduced carbapenem antibacterial to be tested in phase III clinical trials to establish its safety and tolerability in hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia; a suitable testing methodology would be:
options: a prospective, randomized, controlled, double blind, double dummy, multicentre, noninferiority study.
a prospective, randomized, controlled, double blind, multicentre, placebo-controlled superiority study.
questions.correctAnswer: a prospective, randomized, controlled, double blind, double dummy, multicentre, noninferiority study.

questions.question: In which of the following situations the administration of a placebo in the control arm of a clinical study would be the least justified ethically?
options: A clinical trial for a new medication for the control of moderate nausea post-chemotherapy.
A clinical trial for a new quinolone antibacterial for diverticulitis.
A clinical trial for a new quinolone for diabetic foot cellulitis.
A clinical trial for a new, add-on antidepressant medication for acute depressive illness associated with suicidal ideation.
questions.correctAnswer: A clinical trial for a new quinolone for diabetic foot cellulitis.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines the specificity of a diagnostic laboratory test?
options: The ability to identify true positive and false positive results
The ability to identify true negative rate
The ability to identify true positive rate
The ability to identify false positive rate
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to identify true negative rate

Over the course of one year, 5 women were diagnosed with breast cancer, out of a total female study population of 200. Which of the following is a correct conclusion?
options: The prevalence rate of breast cancer in this population is 0.025.
The incidence rate of breast cancer in this population is 2,500 per 100,000 women-years.
The mortality rate of breast cancer in this population is 2,500 per 100,000.
The morbidity rate of breast cancer in this population is 0.25.
questions.correctAnswer: The incidence rate of breast cancer in this population is 2,500 per 100,000 women-years.

A p-value ≤ 0.05 was considered to be statistically significant. Which of the following statistical tests should be used to determine the association between herbal use and each of the independent variables related to the sociodemographic characteristics of the studied diabetic patients?

A drug company is sponsoring studies for a new atypical antipsychotic medication is recruiting for phase 3 interventional trials to test the efficacy and tolerability of the medication in prolonged maintenance therapy of schizophrenic patients who have been in remission for 2 years. An adequate study to accomplish the trial aims would be:
options: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study
a meta-analysis of randomized, double-blind, active comparator, multicenter studies
a prospective nested case control study
questions.correctAnswer: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study

questions.question: A recent meta-analysis study has shown that exposure to proton pump inhibitors (PPI's) might be linked with Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD). The risk estimates were 2.3 for cohort studies (95% CI; 1.72 -3.10) and 1.5 for case-control studies (95% CI, 1.25 -1.75). The overall adjusted risk estimate concluded by the meta-analysis was 1.65. Which of the following statements could NOT be inferred from the performed meta-analysis?
options: Odds ratio suggests an association between CDAD and PPI's chronic therapy.
The incidence of CDAD is increased by at least 50% among users of PPI's vs. nonusers.
A meta-analysis of several observational studies provides higher evidence than a large randomized controlled trial.
The results of the meta-analysis were statistically significant.
questions.correctAnswer: A meta-analysis of several observational studies provides higher evidence than a large randomized controlled trial.

questions.question: A study was conducted to determine the prophylactic efficacy of a standardized cranberry extract in 20 women (mean age 35.2 years; 50.0% were married) with post-coital urinary tract infections who were followed up for 3 and 6 months during treatment. The number of post-coital UTIs in the previous 3 months prior to start the treatment with the cranberry extract was 2.8±1.3 and it was reduced to 0.2+0.5 at month 6 (P<0.0001). What is the research design used in this study?

The data from a randomized clinical study are to be used to estimate the effect strength relevant to the difference in the mean reduction in systolic blood pressure between a new versus a comparator antihypertensive. All of the following statements are true regarding the result of the statistical test involved in that study, EXCEPT:
options: if the P-value is below a predefined limit, the results are designated as 'statistically significant.'
if there was an observed difference in the mean systolic blood pressure with P <0.01, the probability that the two drugs behaved differently due to merely chance is under 1%.
the P-value is a probability which reflects the measure of evidence against the null hypothesis of equality and the larger the p-value the weaker the evidence.
the value of p-statistic correlates with the size and direction of an effect, so a smaller p-value implies a more potent antihypertensive potential.
questions.correctAnswer: if there was an observed difference in the mean systolic blood pressure with P <0.01, the probability that the two drugs behaved differently due to merely chance is under 1%.

questions.question: In the above example, applying the confidence limits, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: A confidence level of 90% means that the confidence interval covers the true value in 90 of 100 blood pressure measurements performed.
The size of the confidence interval depends on the sample size and the standard deviation of the groups so the larger the sample size, the narrower the interval.
Analogous to P-values, statistical significance could be inferred from confidence intervals; however, the latter indicates also the direction and strength of the effect.
The lower and upper confidence limits of the mean difference in systolic blood pressure between the two treatment groups are given in %.
questions.correctAnswer: The lower and upper confidence limits of the mean difference in systolic blood pressure between the two treatment groups are given in %

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true regarding the width of a confidence interval (CI)?
options: The width of a CI decreases as the sample size decreases.
The width of a CI is independent of the sample size.
The width of a CI increases as the sample size decreases.
The width of a CI decreases as the sample size increases.
questions.correctAnswer: The width of a CI decreases as the sample size increases.

questions.question: The number needed to treat (NNT) for amitriptyline in diabetic neuropathic pain was found to be 3, whereas the mixed serotonin nor-adrenaline reuptake inhibitor, duloxetine showed an NNT of about 5. What is the most accurate conclusion that could be drawn from the above data?
options: Amitriptyline and duloxetine are equally efficacious in the treatment of diabetic neuropathy.
A smaller NNT adjusted for the duration of therapy and the background risk implies a more effective treatment with amitriptyline.
Amitriptyline is favorable than duloxetine in controlling long-term peripheral neuropathic pain in diabetic patients.
Duloxetine is a superior therapy for diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
questions.correctAnswer: A smaller NNT adjusted for the duration of therapy and the background risk implies a more effective treatment with amitriptyline.

questions.question: A meta-analysis shows that the number needed to treat for ibuprofen 400 mg to at least cause a 50% pain relief of moderate to severe intensity over six hours, compared with placebo is 2.4 (CI 95% 2.2 to 2.5) and that for acetaminophen 1000 mg is 3.8 (CI 95% 3.4 to 4.4) while that for 10 mg intramuscular morphine is 2.9 (CI 95% 2.6 to 3.6). Based on the aforementioned data, which of the following is true?
options: IM morphine is significantly more effective than acetaminophen for postoperative pain.
The variability in pain response in case of ibuprofen is larger than in case of morphine.
Only 2 out of the 3 interventions show a statistically significant postoperative pain relief.
Morphine IM is significantly less effective than ibuprofen in postoperative pain.
questions.correctAnswer: Morphine IM is significantly less effective than ibuprofen in postoperative pain.

A randomized controlled trial was conducted to investigate the effectiveness of a new treatment for improving the survival of patients with heart failure. A total of 105 patients were randomized to a new treatment, 'A', and a total of 106 were randomized to the control treatment, 'B'. The primary outcome was the overall survival rate. After a median follow-up of 1500 days, the hazard ratio for death in the treatment group was 0.38; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.28 to 0.53. Which of the following is an accurate conclusion of the study?
options: Compared to the control treatment, the new treatment does not confer any survival benefit.
There is a trend of survival benefit on the new treatment, but the results are not statistically significant.
Patients on the new treatment are 62% less likely to die than patients on the control treatment.
Patients in the new treatment group at any time point during the study period were 62% less likely to die than patients in the control group.
questions.correctAnswer: Patients in the new treatment group at any time point during the study period were 62% less likely to die than patients in the control group.
